mechanisms.causal_behavior: Weighting the loss by the inverse error covariance downweights correlated residuals, allowing the model to focus on independent signal and leading to more asymptotically efficient parameter estimates and well-calibrated uncertainty.
mechanisms.math_structure: ℒ = (y - ŷ)^T Σ^{-1} (y - ŷ) + log|Σ| , where Σ is the error covariance matrix (often parameterized as low-rank-plus-diagonal).
mechanisms.consequences: Requires accurate estimation of Σ; iterative computation of Σ^{-1} may increase training cost; ill-conditioned Σ can amplify numerical errors.
anti_patterns: Using a fixed pre-estimated Σ without adaptation during training leads to suboptimal performance; inverting a full Σ without efficient parameterization is computationally prohibitive.

mechanisms.name: knowledge_guided_prompting
mechanisms.abstract_function: Injects domain-specific prior knowledge (e.g., physical propagation or spatial constraints) into a model via learnable prompt vectors or conditioning mechanisms, guiding predictions without explicit feature engineering.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By aligning internal representations with external knowledge through additive or conditioned prompts, the model can exploit known causal structures, reducing reliance on fully data-driven learning.
mechanisms.math_structure: p = Embedding(knowledge_context); h = encoder(x); h' = h + p; output = decoder(h')
mechanisms.consequences: Requires careful design and encoding of prior knowledge; may introduce bias if knowledge is incomplete or misaligned; adds extra parameters.
anti_patterns: Prompts may not transfer across different domains with distinct physical laws.
Over-reliance on static prior harms adaptation to new patterns.

mechanisms.name: adaptive_pathway
mechanisms.abstract_function: Dynamically select and weight a subset of multiple processing pathways based on input features, enabling data-dependent feature aggregation.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: A lightweight router network computes gating weights from the input, and the top-k pathways with the highest weights are activated. The outputs of the selected pathways are aggregated via weighted sum. This allows the model to adapt its computational graph to the varying temporal dynamics of the input, improving generalization across different patterns.
mechanisms.math_structure: Let pathways produce outputs {O1, O2, ..., Om}. Router R gives weights w = softmax(R(input)). Select indices S = top_k(w). Final output = sum_{i in S} w_i * O_i.
mechanisms.consequences: Adds router overhead (extra parameters and forward pass); may cause training instability due to discrete top-k selection; risk of pathway collapse where only one pathway is always chosen.
anti_patterns: Not using top-k (or soft gating) can lead to all pathways always being active, defeating adaptivity and increasing cost.
Router trained with no load-balancing may converge to trivial solutions, ignoring diverse pathways.

mechanisms.name: relative_contrastive_learning
mechanisms.abstract_function: A self-supervised method that learns representations by modeling relative similarities between samples using a learnable distance metric, pulling semantically similar pairs closer and pushing dissimilar pairs apart.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: A learnable distance function captures domain-specific semantic similarities (e.g., rotation invariance). The contrastive loss then uses this distance to define positive/negative pairs, forcing the encoder to produce embeddings where relative ordering of distances reflects semantic relations.
mechanisms.math_structure: L = -log( exp( -d_θ(x_i, x_j) ) / ( ∑_{k∈negatives} exp( -d_θ(x_i, x_k) ) ) ), where d_θ is a learnable distance metric parametrized by θ.
mechanisms.consequences: Extra computational overhead for training the distance network; risk of overfitting the distance metric on small datasets; requires careful initialization and architecture design.
anti_patterns: Overfitting of the distance network when data is limited or noise is high.
Sensitivity to the choice of negative sampling strategy and temperature parameter.

mechanisms.name: disentangled_encoding
mechanisms.abstract_function: Explicitly separate and model different types of dependencies (e.g., temporal order, semantic content, cross-variate interactions) in sequential data to reduce interference and improve representation quality.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By splitting the encoding pathway into separate branches or mechanisms for each dependency type, mutual interference is avoided, and each branch learns a focused representation. This leads to better generalization and interpretability across datasets.
mechanisms.math_structure: Let X ∈ R^{T×C} be input. Disentangled encoding: Z = f_temporal(X) ⊕ f_semantic(X) ⊕ f_cross(X), where each f is a specialized module (e.g., SSM, attention, mixing). ⊕ denotes concatenation or aggregation.
mechanisms.consequences: Increases model complexity and parameter count due to multiple encoding branches; requires careful design to balance branches and avoid over-separation; may need additional regularization.
anti_patterns: Over-separation may lose beneficial interactions between dependencies; if dependencies are weakly defined, separation might introduce bias and degrade performance.

mechanisms.name: linearized_state_space_model
mechanisms.abstract_function: Reduce or eliminate nonlinear activations in state space models to prevent overfitting on data with low semantic density and preserve order information.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Replacing nonlinear components (e.g., tanh, sigmoid) with linear transformations reduces model capacity, acting as a regularizer. This prevents fitting noise and improves generalization on semantically sparse sequences, while maintaining the natural order-preserving property of SSMs.
mechanisms.math_structure: Standard SSM: h_t = σ(W h_{t-1} + U x_t + b). Linearized: h_t = W h_{t-1} + U x_t + b (no σ).
mechanisms.consequences: Reduced expressiveness may limit ability to capture complex nonlinear patterns; can be compensated by increased depth or residual connections; must be tuned to data complexity.
anti_patterns: Only suitable for data with low complexity; may cause underfitting on highly nonlinear data; requires careful validation of linearity assumption.

mechanisms.name: momentum_contrast
mechanisms.abstract_function: Maintain a large, consistent queue of negative representations via a momentum-updated encoder to improve contrastive learning stability and efficiency.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: The momentum encoder slowly tracks the online encoder, producing stable representations that serve as a dynamic memory bank. This provides a large and temporally consistent set of negative samples, reducing representation collapse and enabling training with smaller batch sizes.
mechanisms.math_structure: f_k ← m·f_k + (1-m)·f_q; queue.dequeue(enqueue(f_k(x_k)))
mechanisms.consequences: Increases memory footprint due to the stored queue; momentum coefficient must be tuned carefully; the delayed update can cause staleness in fast-changing data distributions.
anti_patterns: Too large a queue may contain outdated features; momentum close to 1 makes the encoder non-adaptive.

mechanisms.name: contrastive_clustering
mechanisms.abstract_function: Discover underlying groupings in unlabeled data by pulling cluster assignments of transformed views together and pushing apart different clusters via a contrastive objective.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By contrasting instance representations against cluster prototypes or pseudo-labels, the model forces intra-cluster compactness and inter-cluster separability, effectively learning a semantic partition of the data space.
mechanisms.math_structure: p_i = softmax(Z·C); L = -Σ_i log[ exp(p_i·c_yi/τ) / Σ_j exp(p_i·c_j/τ) ]
mechanisms.consequences: Requires specifying the number of clusters a priori; susceptible to trivial solutions (all instances in one cluster) and sensitivity to initialization.
anti_patterns: Unbalanced cluster sizes can bias the loss; updating cluster centroids too frequently leads to instability.

mechanisms.name: soft_clustering_for_hyperedge_discovery
mechanisms.abstract_function: Unsupervisedly infer a latent hypergraph structure from node-level observations by modeling each hyperedge as a cluster of correlated nodes, using a differentiable soft assignment.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Soft clustering iteratively assigns each node a probability of belonging to each hyperedge, capturing higher-order correlations without requiring explicit connectivity. The inferred hypergraph enables hypergraph neural networks to model group interactions that would be lost in pairwise graphs.
mechanisms.math_structure: For each hyperedge e, node v's membership probability: p_{v,e} = softmax(MLP(h_v))_e. Update cluster centroids via weighted aggregation. The process is repeated to refine assignments.
mechanisms.consequences: Requires pre-specifying number of hyperedges; may be computationally expensive if many hyperedges; sensitive to initialization of cluster parameters.
anti_patterns: Fixing hyperedge count too low leads to underfitting high-order interactions; too high causes overfitting noise.
Soft assignment may collapse to trivial solutions if not regularized or if node features are uninformative.

mechanisms.name: differentiable_k_subset_sampling
mechanisms.abstract_function: Sample a discrete subset of exactly k elements from a set in a fully differentiable manner, enabling gradient-based optimization of subset selection within neural networks.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By relaxing the discrete sampling into a continuous approximation (e.g., Gumbel-Softmax with temperature annealing), gradients can flow through the sampling operation, allowing a neural network to learn to select a sparse set of elements (e.g., nodes for a hyperedge) while maintaining discreteness during forward pass.
mechanisms.math_structure: Given logits π_i for i=1..N, sample: y_i = softmax((log π_i + g_i)/τ) where g_i ~ Gumbel(0,1). Then perturb top-k selection via a relaxation like Gumbel-Sinkhorn or subset sampling (e.g., from Minervini et al. 2023).
mechanisms.consequences: Temperature annealing is required to balance gradient quality and sample discreteness; can suffer from high variance at low temperature; may require careful hyperparameter tuning.
anti_patterns: Using too low temperature makes gradients vanish; too high makes samples nearly uniform, losing sparsity.
If k is large relative to N, the sampling may become unstable or lose meaningful subset selection.

mechanisms.name: node_adaptive_low_rank_layer
mechanisms.abstract_function: Enhance model flexibility by applying low-rank transformations independently to each element (e.g., node, channel) of a multi-element representation, enabling efficient element-specific adaptation with few extra parameters.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: For each element i, a low-rank matrix W_i = U_i V_i^T is applied to shared input features, adapting them to element-specific dynamics. This captures variations across elements without dramatically increasing parameters, as the low-rank decomposition keeps per-element parameters O(r) instead of O(d^2).
mechanisms.math_structure: h_i' = (U_i V_i^T) h + b_i, where U_i∈R^{d×r}, V_i∈R^{d×r}, r << d, h shared feature.
mechanisms.consequences: Adds per-element parameters but efficient due to low rank; may need sufficient per-element data to avoid overfitting.
anti_patterns: Using shared low-rank bases across all elements may not capture extreme heterogeneity; over-regularization if rank too low.

mechanisms.name: multi_objective_reinforcement_learning
mechanisms.abstract_function: Optimize multiple conflicting objectives by learning a policy that balances trade-offs, either from explicit preferences or inferred from data.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By formulating a multi-objective reward function and using RL to maximize a scalarized reward (e.g., via linear weighting or Pareto front learning), the policy adapts to varying objective preferences.
mechanisms.math_structure: J(θ) = E[∑_t γ^t Σ_i w_i * r_i(s_t, a_t)]
mechanisms.consequences: Increased training complexity due to multiple objectives; need for proper weighting or preference inference; potential instability.
anti_patterns: Over-reliance on predefined weights may bias the policy towards a single objective, ignoring the Pareto front.
Preference inference from few samples can be brittle if the sample distribution is not representative.

mechanisms.name: cluster_conditional_mixture_of_experts
mechanisms.abstract_function: Trains multiple expert models where each expert specializes on a subset of data determined by clustering, and a cluster-conditional gating network assigns each input to the most relevant expert based on its cluster assignment, enabling task-specific customization and reducing negative transfer from irrelevant data.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By partitioning the input data into clusters of semantically similar samples and training each expert only on its assigned cluster, the model learns specialized features for each data mode. The cluster-conditional gate ensures that during inference or downstream fine-tuning, inputs are routed to the expert with the most similar training distribution, thus avoiding negative transfer from irrelevant pre-training data and improving downstream performance.
mechanisms.math_structure: Let clustering function C(x) map input x to a cluster index k ∈ {1,...,K}. Expert output E_k(x) for cluster k. Gating output G(x) = one-hot(argmax_k C(x)), final output = Σ_k G_k(x) * E_k(x) (hard assignment) or using soft gating based on cluster probabilities.
mechanisms.consequences: Increases training complexity due to need for clustering and expert management; requires careful balancing of expert capacities to avoid underutilization; may introduce overhead in gate computation; clustering step may be sensitive to hyperparameters.
anti_patterns: Ignoring cluster imbalance (some experts may receive very few samples)
Using a fixed clustering that does not adapt during training can lead to suboptimal specialization

mechanisms.name: gumbel_softmax_topk_selection
mechanisms.abstract_function: Differentiably selects the top-k most relevant elements from a set of candidates using Gumbel-Softmax sampling, enabling sparse and noise-resistant information aggregation.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By adding Gumbel noise to logits and applying softmax with temperature τ, the mechanism produces a differentiable approximation to discrete top-k selection. The straight-through estimator allows gradient flow through the hard selection, enabling end-to-end training. This filters out irrelevant or noisy candidates, improving the robustness of aggregated representations.
mechanisms.math_structure: For each query, compute logits z_i ∈ ℝ^N. Let g_i = -log(-log(U_i)), U_i~Uniform(0,1). Sample scores: s_i = softmax((z_i + g_i)/τ). Hard top-k: indices = argsort(s)[:k]; y_hard = one_hot(indices). Forward uses y_hard; backward uses softmax gradient via straight-through: ∂L/∂z ≈ ∂L/∂y_hard · ∂y_hard/∂s · ∂s/∂z.
mechanisms.consequences: Computationally overhead from Gumbel sampling and top-k sorting; requires careful tuning of temperature τ for gradient quality; straight-through gradient can be biased; may sacrifice information from non-selected elements.
anti_patterns: Setting τ too low leads to near-zero gradients; setting τ too high yields uniform selection, losing sparsity.
Using a fixed k without adaptive adjustment may discard important but low-confidence elements.

mechanisms.name: asymmetric_reweighting_loss
mechanisms.abstract_function: Mitigates label imbalance—both positive-negative skew and long-tail distribution—by applying sample-specific weights modulated by asymmetric focusing factors and effective number of samples.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: The loss assigns different focusing factors γ_pos > γ_neg to positive and negative samples, shifting model attention toward rare positive examples. Additionally, it weights each class by the inverse of its effective number (volume-based heuristic), reducing the impact of over-represented head classes. This jointly addresses severe class imbalance and long-tailed patterns.
mechanisms.math_structure: L = - Σ_{c} w_c [ λ_+ (1-p_c)^{γ_+} log(p_c) if c is positive, else λ_- (1-p_c)^{γ_-} log(1-p_c) ], where w_c = (1-β) / (1-β^{n_c}) with n_c being the number of samples in class c and β a hyperparameter.
mechanisms.consequences: Introduces two additional hyperparameters (γ_pos, γ_neg) and the effective number parameter β; may over-suppress negative gradients, degrading recall for non-target classes; computational cost negligible.
anti_patterns: Setting γ_pos too large can lead to overfitting on rare positives; γ_neg too small undermines imbalance correction.
Assuming the effective number formula works universally—may fail when class frequencies are highly non-uniform across validation splits.

mechanisms.name: distribution_aware_experience_replay
mechanisms.abstract_function: Selectively replay training samples based on distribution distance between historical and current data to mitigate catastrophic forgetting under distribution shift and evolving structure.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Using Wasserstein distance to quantify distribution shift between historical and new node data; nodes with small distance are considered stable (for consolidation), large distance indicate changing nodes (for adaptation). Replaying only stable nodes avoids overfitting to outdated patterns, while training on changing nodes adapts to new dynamics.
mechanisms.math_structure: Compute Wasserstein distance W(μ_hist, μ_new) for each node; threshold to decide stable/changing; loss = L_consolidation(stable) + L_adaptation(changing+new)
mechanisms.consequences: Requires storing historical node representations or statistics; additional computation for Wasserstein distance; may not work well when all nodes change significantly.
anti_patterns: Treating all nodes equally causes forgetting or overfitting
Assuming Wasserstein distance captures all aspects of distribution shift may ignore label shift

mechanisms.name: quadtree_spatial_partitioning
mechanisms.abstract_function: Adaptively partition a 2D space into quadrants of varying granularity based on data density, enabling multi-scale spatial representation.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By recursively subdividing dense regions into finer tiles, the structure captures spatial non-uniformity and balances representation across areas with varying densities, improving spatial modeling capacity.
mechanisms.math_structure: Define region R; if count(points_in_R) > threshold: split R into 4 equal quadrants; repeat recursively.
mechanisms.consequences: Simple and memory efficient; may produce unbalanced tree depth; loses spatial continuity between adjacent quadrants.
anti_patterns: Using fixed grid partitions for highly heterogeneous distributions, which collapses dense areas into few cells.
Ignoring spatial continuity across quadrants, which breaks smoothness priors.

mechanisms.name: coarse_to_fine_prediction
mechanisms.abstract_function: Decompose a prediction task into hierarchical stages: first infer a coarse region, then predict the precise label or location within that region.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Narrowing the search space at each stage simplifies learning; the coarse prediction provides contextual prior that disambiguates fine-grained classes, improving accuracy and handling class imbalance.
mechanisms.math_structure: Stage1: argmax_{c} P(region=c | X); Stage2: argmax_{f} P(label=f | region=c, X).
mechanisms.consequences: Increased inference latency due to multi-step; error propagation from coarse stage; requires well-defined coarse labels that align with the fine task.
anti_patterns: Using coarse regions that aggregate semantically dissimilar labels, causing ambiguous fine-task conditioning.
Training stages independently without end-to-end learning, leading to suboptimal joint optimization.

mechanisms.name: relational_spatial_encoding
mechanisms.abstract_function: Encode spatial positions of entities based on their relative relationships (e.g., order, distance) to other entities rather than absolute coordinates, enabling invariant spatial representation that generalizes across different coordinate systems.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By encoding positions relative to neighbors rather than absolute coordinates, the representation becomes invariant to translation and rotation in the spatial coordinate system. This allows the model to focus on local spatial layout, improving generalization to unseen spatial arrangements and enabling the use of local aggregation operations.
mechanisms.math_structure: For entity i, its spatial encoding is a function of its relations to others: e_i = aggregate_{j in neighbors} f( rel(i,j) ), where rel(i,j) can be a tuple of signed distance, order, etc. (e.g., longitudinal position = signed distance from vehicle i to reference vehicle j).
mechanisms.consequences: Increased computational cost when number of entities is large due to pairwise relation computation; may lose global spatial context if relations are only local.
anti_patterns: Not suitable when global absolute coordinates are critical (e.g., GPS-based localization)
May suffer from ambiguity if relative relations are incomplete

mechanisms.name: equivalence_based_scenario_merging
mechanisms.abstract_function: Reduce redundancy in a set of scenarios by grouping those that are semantically equivalent under a defined equivalence relation (e.g., same relational structure), thereby improving reasoning efficiency without loss of coverage.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By defining an equivalence relation on scenarios (e.g., based on same vehicle relationships), merging equivalent scenarios compresses the state space while preserving all distinct relational patterns. This reduces the number of cases to consider during reasoning, enabling faster inference with identical logical conclusions.
mechanisms.math_structure: Let S be the set of all possible scenarios. Define equivalence relation ~ such that s1 ~ s2 if they share the same set of relational constraints. Then the reduced scenario set is S/~ (set of equivalence classes). Reasoning is performed on each class representative.
mechanisms.consequences: May lose fine-grained details if equivalence relation is too coarse; requires careful definition of equivalence to avoid missing critical differences.
anti_patterns: Avoid merging scenarios that differ in safety-critical properties
Equivalence relation must be sound with respect to the reasoning goals

mechanisms.name: heterogeneous_graph_neural_network
mechanisms.abstract_function: Process graph-structured data composed of multiple types of nodes and edges with specialized transformation functions per type.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By assigning distinct feature transformation and aggregation functions to different node/edge types, the model captures type-specific patterns and interactions while maintaining a unified graph representation.
mechanisms.math_structure: H_i^{(l+1)} = Agg_{j \in N(i)} \phi_{type(i,j)}(h_i^{(l)}, h_j^{(l)}, e_{ij})
mechanisms.consequences: Increased model complexity and number of parameters due to type-specific functions; requires explicit type annotations.
anti_patterns: Ignoring type heterogeneity (treating all nodes as same) leads to suboptimal performance
Over-typing (too many fine-grained types) causes data sparsity

mechanisms.name: hierarchical_graph_neural_network
mechanisms.abstract_function: Aggregate and pool graph information across multiple spatial scales to capture both local and global structure.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Through hierarchical pooling and coarsening, the network compresses long-range dependencies into coarser levels, enabling efficient capture of global patterns.
mechanisms.math_structure: Z = Readout(Pool(GCN(X, A)))
mechanisms.consequences: Loss of fine-grained information during pooling; careful design needed to ensure reversible or meaningful coarsening.
anti_patterns: Excessive pooling can destroy essential local connectivity
Unbalanced hierarchies can bias towards certain scales

mechanisms.name: weight_sharing
mechanisms.abstract_function: Reuse the same set of model parameters across different components, tasks, or environments to enforce consistency and enable zero-shot transfer.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By tying weights, the model is forced to learn features that are invariant across different conditions, reducing overfitting to any single scenario and enabling generalization.
mechanisms.math_structure: Parameter vector \theta is shared: L(\theta) = \sum_{t} L_t(\theta), where t indexes different tasks/environments.
mechanisms.consequences: Reduces number of parameters and computational cost; may limit flexibility if tasks are too diverse.
anti_patterns: Sharing weights across highly disparate tasks can cause negative transfer
Careful selection of sharing scope required

mechanisms.name: domain_randomization
mechanisms.abstract_function: Introduce randomized variations in simulation or training environment parameters to improve robustness and generalization to unseen conditions.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By exposing the model to a wide range of randomized scenarios during training, it learns to ignore irrelevant variations and focus on invariant features, thereby enhancing zero-shot transfer.
mechanisms.math_structure: At each episode, sample environment parameters from a randomization distribution p(\phi), train policy \pi on environment E(\phi).
mechanisms.consequences: Requires extensive randomization distribution design; may increase training time and sample complexity.
anti_patterns: Over-randomization can wash out useful correlations
Under-randomization limits generalization

mechanisms.name: spatial_distance_weighted_reward
mechanisms.abstract_function: Weight the reward contribution of each entity by a monotonic function of its spatial distance to a reference point, to encourage spatially-aware prioritization.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By assigning higher weights to closer or farther entities via a distance transformation (e.g., log distance), the reward signal becomes spatially modulated, enabling adaptive trade-offs between local and global objectives.
mechanisms.math_structure: R_i = w(d_i) * r_i, with w(d_i) = 1 / log(d_i + \epsilon) or similar, where d_i is distance to reference.
mechanisms.consequences: Introduces continuous spatial awareness; may require careful tuning of the weighting function to avoid unintended bias.
anti_patterns: Using unbounded weighting (e.g., inverse distance) can cause instability
Log distance may underweight very close entities

mechanisms.name: hard_negative_synthesis_for_contrastive_learning
mechanisms.abstract_function: Generate synthetic hard negative samples using pretrained generative models to enhance the discriminative capabilities of contrastive representation learning across modalities or within a single domain.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Pretrained generative models produce negative samples that are semantically close to positives but differ in fine-grained compositional details. The contrastive objective must distinguish these hard negatives, forcing the encoder to learn representations that capture subtle compositional semantics, improving compositional reasoning and zero-shot transfer.
mechanisms.math_structure: Contrastive loss: L = -log(exp(sim(z_i,z_j)/τ) / (Σ_{positive} exp(sim(z_i,z_k)/τ) + Σ_{synthetic_hard_negative} exp(sim(z_i,z_neg)/τ))). Negative generation: x_neg = G(c_neg), where c_neg is a perturbed caption and G is a text-to-image generator.
mechanisms.consequences: Requires access to high-quality generative models, increasing computational cost and introducing generation artifacts that may degrade performance if negatives are unrealistic or too easy.
anti_patterns: Over-reliance on generative model quality; if generated negatives are too similar to positives or too noisy, they can hinder learning rather than help.
Generation latency may become a training bottleneck, especially for large-scale datasets.

mechanisms.name: wavelet_decomposition
mechanisms.abstract_function: Decompose a signal into multiple frequency-band components using wavelet transforms, enabling multi-scale analysis in both time and frequency domains.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Wavelet transforms use scaled and shifted versions of a mother wavelet to compute approximation and detail coefficients, capturing low-frequency trends and high-frequency fluctuations at multiple resolutions, which allows the model to separate complex temporal patterns.
mechanisms.math_structure: W_j(t) = sum_tau x(tau) * psi_{j,tau}(t); approximation A_j and detail D_j at each level j.
mechanisms.consequences: Increased dimensionality due to multiple coefficient series; computational cost of transform; possible boundary effects on short sequences.
anti_patterns: Applying only one-level decomposition may miss fine-grained patterns.
Using on very short sequences where boundary effects dominate.
Using inappropriate wavelet basis that does not match data characteristics may lead to poor decomposition.
Applying fixed decomposition levels without considering data length can cause excessive or insufficient detail.

mechanisms.name: weight_invariant_path_index
mechanisms.abstract_function: Precompute a set of structurally defined paths (e.g., based on static topological attributes) in a graph with dynamically changing edge weights; these paths remain unaffected by weight variations and provide lower-bound distance estimates between boundary vertices, enabling efficient query processing and low index maintenance.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By precomputing paths using static (weight-invariant) attributes, the index is robust to dynamic weight changes → no online update required for weight shifts → the lower bounds derived from these paths guide distributed pruning and refinement, reducing search space without recomputing full paths.
mechanisms.math_structure: Given graph G partitioned into subgraphs {G_i} with boundary vertex sets B_i. For each subgraph G_i and each pair (u,v) ∈ B_i, compute: BoundingPath(u,v) = shortest_path_in_static_sense(u, v; G_i, cost_static); store weight w_b(u,v) = cost_static(BoundingPath) and the path itself. Index provides lower bounds for any shortest path between u,v in dynamic G.
mechanisms.consequences: Requires precomputation and storage of bounding paths (mitigated by tree-based compression); lower bound tightness depends on correlation between static and dynamic weights; not suitable when graph structure (edges/nodes) changes frequently.
anti_patterns: If dynamic weights are completely uncorrelated with static attributes, lower bounds become too loose to prune effectively.
Precomputation cost may be prohibitive for graphs that undergo structural updates (node/edge addition/deletion).

mechanisms.name: channel_aligned_attention
mechanisms.abstract_function: An attention mechanism that simultaneously models both temporal dependencies among time steps and dynamical correlations among multiple variables (channels) by computing attention over both dimensions.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Computing attention over both time and channel dimensions enables the model to capture inter-variable interactions and temporal patterns jointly, leveraging complementary information to improve forecasting accuracy under high-dimensional and heterogeneous multivariate settings.
mechanisms.math_structure: Given input X ∈ ℝ^{B×T×C}, project to Q, K, V ∈ ℝ^{B×T×C} via linear layers. Compute attention score A = softmax( (Q ⊗ K) / √d ) where ⊗ represents an interaction over both T and C (e.g., flatten or bilinear product), then output = A · V.
mechanisms.consequences: Quadratic compute cost in (T×C) making it expensive for large T or C; risk of overfitting to noise, necessitating smoothing techniques.
anti_patterns: Directly applying to very large channel dimensions may cause memory explosion.
Ignoring smoothing of attention inputs leads to poor robustness on noisy datasets.

mechanisms.name: token_blend_module
mechanisms.abstract_function: Generates multi-scale token representations by merging adjacent tokens within the same attention head, producing coarser tokens at different resolutions while preserving local continuity.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Merging adjacent tokens reduces sequence length and captures larger-scale patterns, enabling the model to leverage both fine-grained and coarse-grained information without losing the inherent temporal order.
mechanisms.math_structure: For each head, given token sequence of length L, apply a merge operation (e.g., average or sum) over non-overlapping windows of size k to produce new tokens of length L/k.
mechanisms.consequences: Reduces computational cost by decreasing token count; may lose fine-grained details if merging is too aggressive; requires careful selection of merge window size.
anti_patterns: Over-merging eliminates subtle patterns necessary for short-term forecasting.
Hard to apply when sequence length is not divisible by merge factor.

mechanisms.name: exponential_smoothing_attention
mechanisms.abstract_function: Applies exponential moving average to queries and keys prior to attention computation to suppress high-frequency noise and stabilize the attention distribution.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Smoothing each query and key along the time dimension reduces random fluctuations, allowing attention to focus on consistent temporal patterns and improving robustness against noisy inputs.
mechanisms.math_structure: Q̂_t = α·Q_t + (1-α)·Q̂_{t-1},  K̂_t = α·K_t + (1-α)·K̂_{t-1}, where α ∈ (0,1) is a smoothing factor.
mechanisms.consequences: Negligible computational overhead; may blur sharp transitions if α is too small; requires tuning of smoothing coefficient.
anti_patterns: Excessive smoothing can destroy sudden but meaningful changes (e.g., changepoints).
Incompatible with tasks relying on abrupt pattern shifts.

mechanisms.name: uncertainty_weighted_loss
mechanisms.abstract_function: A loss function that weights each individual prediction by its estimated uncertainty, assigning higher importance to more certain predictions and down-weighting uncertain ones to improve generalization.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By incorporating a separate uncertainty estimate (e.g., learned variance), the loss automatically adapts to per-sample prediction difficulty, reducing the impact of noisy or out-of-distribution points during training.
mechanisms.math_structure: L = Σ_i [ 0.5·exp(-s_i)·(y_i - ŷ_i)² + 0.5·s_i ] (for Gaussian likelihood), where s_i = log(σ_i²) is log-variance learned jointly with the prediction.
mechanisms.consequences: Requires estimating uncertainty per prediction, doubling output dimension; may slow training; provides inherent regularization and improved calibration.
anti_patterns: If uncertainty estimates are inaccurate, the weighting can harm performance.
Does not address all types of distribution shift (e.g., covariate shift without variance change).

mechanisms.name: prototype_bank
mechanisms.abstract_function: Constructs a compact set of representative prototypes from a large collection of encoded source features via clustering, enabling retrieval and weighted aggregation of relevant patterns for target queries to support few-shot learning or domain adaptation.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By clustering large sets of source-domain embeddings into a compact set of prototype vectors, the bank captures common patterns. During inference, target embeddings attend to these prototypes via similarity, enabling knowledge transfer and reducing domain shift effects. The weighted aggregation of prototypes provides a robust representation for the target task.
mechanisms.math_structure: Let Z_s = {z₁,...,z_N} be source embeddings. Apply k-means → K prototypes {c₁,...,c_K}. For query q, compute attention weights a_i = softmax(sim(q, c_i)). Aggregate: r = Σ_i a_i * c_i.
mechanisms.consequences: Requires precomputation and storage of prototypes; clustering quality impacts performance; assumes source and target distributions share common patterns; may not generalize well under severe distribution shift.
anti_patterns: Insufficient number of prototypes may fail to capture fine-grained patterns.
If source and target distributions diverge, prototypes become uninformative and degrade performance.

mechanisms.name: reptile
mechanisms.abstract_function: An outer-loop meta-learning algorithm that learns a model initialization enabling fast adaptation to new tasks with a small number of gradient steps, by iteratively pulling the initialization toward task-specific optimums.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By repeatedly sampling tasks, performing few-step gradient updates, and moving the initialization towards the updated parameters, Reptile learns a parameter initialization that is close to task-specific minima. This allows rapid adaptation to new tasks with limited data, as the model can quickly converge from the initialization.
mechanisms.math_structure: For each iteration: sample task T_i, initialize θ. Perform k gradient descent steps: θ_k = θ - α ∇ L_T_i(θ). Update global parameters: θ = θ + β (θ_k - θ).
mechanisms.consequences: Requires a distribution of tasks; computationally expensive due to inner loops; sensitive to inner learning rate and number of steps; may not converge well for highly diverse tasks.
anti_patterns: Can be unstable if task distribution is too diverse.
Requires careful tuning of inner steps and outer learning rate; too many inner steps may cause overfitting to sampled tasks.

mechanisms.name: vector_quantized_disentanglement
mechanisms.abstract_function: Separates input data into invariant and time-varying components by discretizing the time-varying part via vector quantization, enabling robust generalization under distribution shifts.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By encoding time-varying environments into discrete codes and separating them from invariant representation, the model blocks back-door paths from confounding temporal factors, forcing the invariant part to be context-independent and improving out-of-distribution generalization.
mechanisms.math_structure: z_t = Enc(x_t); e_c from codebook; q(z_t) = argmin_c ||z_t - e_c||; define invariant entity as z_t - e_c (or separate via straight-through); environment represented by discrete code e_c.
mechanisms.consequences: Additional memory for codebook; potential information loss due to quantization; training instability from straight-through gradient estimator; extra hyperparameter (codebook size).
anti_patterns: When temporal environments are continuous and fine-grained, discrete quantization may lose essential nuance.
Large codebook leads to sparse usage; small codebook causes mode collapse.

mechanisms.name: hodge_laplacian_edge_convolution
mechanisms.abstract_function: Performs convolution on edge features of a graph using the Hodge-Laplacian operator to model propagation of causal effects along spatial relations in a higher-order manner.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: The Hodge-Laplacian on 1-chains captures how edge signals diffuse across the graph; applying it as a convolutional filter allows ripple effects of causal relations (e.g., traffic accidents) to propagate spatially over time, modeling dynamic spatial causality.
mechanisms.math_structure: Given edge feature matrix E ∈ ℝ^{|E|×d}, Hodge-Laplacian L₁ ∈ ℝ^{|E|×|E|}, filter g, output = (L₁ * E) * g (with appropriate normalization).
mechanisms.consequences: Higher memory and compute cost than node-level convolution; requires constructing the Hodge-Laplacian; may need special normalization for stability.
anti_patterns: Not beneficial when edge-level dynamics are absent or graph is static.
Excessive edge dimension can blow up memory (|E| quadratic in nodes).

mechanisms.name: sparse_soft_vector_quantization
mechanisms.abstract_function: Maps continuous feature vectors to a sparse convex combination of learnable codebook elements, enabling differentiable quantization that balances noise reduction and detail preservation.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Hard vector quantization is non-differentiable and limits representational capacity. By replacing hard argmin with a sparse linear combination of codebook vectors (via a top-k softmax over MLP-generated coefficients), gradients flow through the quantization step, and sparsity forces the model to retain only the most salient recurring patterns while suppressing noise. The large codebook with MLP-based selection keeps computation manageable.
mechanisms.math_structure: Let z be input, C = {e_1,...,e_K} codebook. Compute w = softmax(MLP(z)). Apply top-k mask: w' = w ⊙ mask_topk(w, k). Output = Σ_i w'_i * e_i.
mechanisms.consequences: Adds codebook and MLP training cost; requires tuning sparsity level k and codebook size; may over-smooth if sparsity is too high, losing fine-grained details.
anti_patterns: Using too small codebook collapses representation to trivial prototypes.
Setting sparsity too low fails to filter noise, reducing denoising effect.

mechanisms.name: metadata_prediction_pretraining
mechanisms.abstract_function: Predicts auxiliary continuous attributes derived from the sample's metadata as a self-supervised pretext task to inject domain knowledge into representations.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By forcing the model to predict metadata (e.g., geographic coordinates) from input features, the encoder learns to extract features that correlate with the metadata, thus incorporating domain-specific structural priors into the representation.
mechanisms.math_structure: L = MSE( f_θ(x_i), y_i^{meta} )
mechanisms.consequences: Requires metadata availability; representation may overfit to metadata-specific features; limited if metadata is noisy or irrelevant.
anti_patterns: Metadata must be reasonably correlated with downstream tasks; otherwise may bias representations away from useful features.

mechanisms.name: positional_encoding
mechanisms.abstract_function: Inject information about the position of each element in a sequence into the input representations, enabling a sequence model to use order information, typically via fixed sinusoidal functions or learned embeddings.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By adding position-specific signals to input embeddings, the model can differentiate between same values at different positions, which is crucial for tasks where order matters. Sinusoidal encoding provides inductive bias for relative positions.
mechanisms.math_structure: PE(pos,2i)=sin(pos/10000^(2i/d_model)), PE(pos,2i+1)=cos(pos/10000^(2i/d_model)) or E_learned ∈ R^(L×d).
mechanisms.consequences: Fixed sinusoidal encoding may not be optimal for some tasks; learned positional embeddings require training and may not generalize to unseen lengths; adding positional information can increase model capacity.
anti_patterns: Using learned positional embeddings without proper regularization for variable length sequences; applying positional encoding to tasks where order is irrelevant.

mechanisms.name: collaborative_latent_reconstruction
mechanisms.abstract_function: Reconstruct a target representation by fusing latent embeddings from multiple sources (e.g., modalities or views), forcing the encoder to capture shared and generalized knowledge across sources.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By constructing a comprehensive reconstruction target from multiple latent sources, the encoder must learn to extract common patterns across sources, leading to more robust and transferable representations.
mechanisms.math_structure: Let Z = {Z1, Z2, ..., Zk} be latent representations from k sources. Target T = aggregate(Z). Reconstruction loss L = MSE(M(X_masked), T) or L = -I(T; Z).
mechanisms.consequences: Increases computational cost due to multi-source aggregation and potential need for alignment; performance depends on the relevance of the sources.
anti_patterns: Fusing irrelevant sources may introduce noise and degrade representations.
Requires careful design of aggregation function to avoid trivial solutions.

mechanisms.name: mutual_information_reconstruction_loss
mechanisms.abstract_function: Use mutual information as a reconstruction objective to differentiate between exclusive knowledge from individual targets and shared knowledge among multiple targets, promoting disentangled representations.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Maximizing the mutual information between the reconstructed target and the shared source while minimizing it for exclusive sources encourages the encoder to separate common and unique features.
mechanisms.math_structure: L = -α I(T_shared; Z_shared) + β Σ_i I(T_exclusive_i; Z_i), where T_shared and T_exclusive_i are separated targets.
mechanisms.consequences: Estimating mutual information is challenging and often requires variational approximations; training may be unstable with small batch sizes.
anti_patterns: Poor mutual information estimation can lead to trivial solutions.
May conflict with other loss components if hyperparameters are not tuned.

mechanisms.name: neighborhood_aggregation
mechanisms.abstract_function: Aggregates feature information from local neighbors in a graph to update node representations, enabling the capture of structural context.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By defining a local neighborhood for each node and aggregating features from those neighbors (e.g., mean, sum, or max pooling), the node's updated representation encodes both its own features and the structural patterns of its local subgraph. This allows the model to learn relational dependencies that are invariant to node ordering and generalizable across different graph structures.
mechanisms.consequences: Computationally scales with node degree and number of layers; may lead to oversmoothing in deep architectures; requires efficient sampling for large graphs.
anti_patterns: Using a fixed aggregation function (e.g., mean) on graphs with highly varying node degrees without normalization can cause unstable representations.
Ignoring edge attributes or directional information may lose critical relational signals.

mechanisms.name: multi_task_learning
mechanisms.abstract_function: Simultaneously learns multiple related tasks by sharing a common representation, improving generalization and data efficiency across tasks.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By sharing lower-level features among tasks (e.g., shared hidden layers), the model leverages statistical strength from tasks with abundant labels to regularize tasks with scarce labels, reducing overfitting and enabling better generalization to unseen task combinations.
mechanisms.math_structure: L_total = Σ_{t=1}^{T} α_t L_t( f_shared(x), y_t )
mechanisms.consequences: Requires careful tuning of task weights α_t; negative transfer may occur if tasks are unrelated; increases model capacity and training complexity.
anti_patterns: Forcing all tasks to share all parameters without task-specific heads can lead to poor performance on tasks with conflicting objectives.
Using equal task weights when label volumes vary dramatically may bias training toward the task with more data.

mechanisms.name: hourglass_encoder_decoder_with_skip_connections
mechanisms.abstract_function: A hierarchical architecture that progressively downsamples and upsamples representations across scales, with skip connections preserving fine details, to fuse multi-scale features for sequence modeling.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Downsampling compresses the temporal dimension to capture coarse-grained context, upsampling recovers resolution, and skip connections pass high-resolution features from encoder to decoder, enabling the model to jointly reason over multiple scales and long-range dependencies.
mechanisms.math_structure: Encoder: x_l = f_l(Pooling(x_{l-1})); Decoder: y_{l-1} = g_l(Upsample(y_l) + SkipConnection(x_l))
mechanisms.consequences: Increased memory and computational cost due to multi-scale processing and skip connections; careful design of pooling/upsampling ratios needed to avoid detail loss or aliasing.
anti_patterns: Overly aggressive downsampling may discard critical fine-grained patterns; too many skip connections can cause redundancy and hinder hierarchical abstraction.

mechanisms.name: dimension_separated_self_attention
mechanisms.abstract_function: Applies self-attention independently to each axis (e.g., time and space) of a multi-dimensional sequence, allowing efficient capture of long-range dependencies within each dimension while keeping computational cost tractable.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By attending over only one dimension at a time, the mechanism reduces the quadratic complexity from O(N*M) to O(N+M) per head (where N, M are dimension sizes), and each attention head learns pairwise relations unique to that axis, enabling focused long-range mixing.
mechanisms.math_structure: For time axis: Attn_t = softmax(Q_t K_t^T / sqrt(d)) V_t; For space axis: Attn_s = softmax(Q_s K_s^T / sqrt(d)) V_s
mechanisms.consequences: Neglects cross-dimensional interactions, requiring an additional fusion mechanism; may underperform when dimensions are highly correlated (e.g., spatio-temporal points coupled).
anti_patterns: Applying to dimensions with vastly different lengths without adaptive scaling can lead to numerical instability; ignoring inter-axis interactions may lose critical dependencies.

mechanisms.name: cross_modal_context_fusion_block
mechanisms.abstract_function: A plug-in module that adaptively fuses representations from two distinct modalities or feature subspaces (e.g., spatial and temporal) through learned gating or attention, enabling complementary information exchange.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Estimates a soft gate or cross-attention map between the two feature sets, weighting contributions from each source, so that informative signals propagate and redundant or conflicting noise is suppressed, leading to enriched joint representations.
mechanisms.math_structure: Let S, T be spatial and temporal features. Gate = sigmoid(W[s;T] + b); Fused = Gate * S + (1-Gate) * T (or cross-attention: F = CrossAttn(S, T))
mechanisms.consequences: Adds extra parameters and computational overhead; gate designs must avoid collapse (e.g., always selecting one source) and require careful initialization.
anti_patterns: Overly complex fusion (e.g., multi-layer cross-attention) may overfit when data is limited; naive additive fusion can wash out fine-grained per-dimension patterns.

mechanisms.name: cyclic_normalization
mechanisms.abstract_function: Normalize time series within each fixed-length cycle (period) to reduce inter-cycle non-stationarity while preserving intra-cycle patterns, with a reversible de-normalization step for forecasting.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By partitioning the time series into cycles of known period and computing local mean and standard deviation per cycle, the normalized series has reduced distribution shift across cycles. The model learns from the normalized data, then the de-normalization reinstates the original scale and offsets, improving forecast accuracy especially for peak patterns.
mechanisms.math_structure: For a cycle of length P: μ_i = mean(x_{i,1:P}), σ_i = std(x_{i,1:P}); normalized: x'_{i,j} = (x_{i,j} - μ_i) / σ_i; denormalized: ŷ_{i,j} = ŷ'_{i,j} * σ_i + μ_i.
mechanisms.consequences: Requires known period length; adds negligible computational overhead for per-cycle statistics; may reduce representational capacity if cycle statistics are not stationary.
anti_patterns: Not suitable for non-periodic series; may degrade performance if period length is incorrectly specified.

mechanisms.name: convolution
mechanisms.abstract_function: Extract local spatial patterns by sliding a learned kernel over an input grid, computing weighted sums over local neighborhoods.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Local connectivity and weight sharing induce translation invariance and capture spatially correlated features by repeatedly applying the same kernel across all positions.
mechanisms.math_structure: (I * K)(x,y) = sum_i sum_j I(x-i, y-j) * K(i,j)
mechanisms.consequences: Limited receptive field without stacking layers; computational cost scales with kernel size and input dimensions; assumes translation invariance.
anti_patterns: Applying to data without spatial smoothness; using large kernels without considering memory/overfitting.

mechanisms.name: auxiliary_density_prediction
mechanisms.abstract_function: Predict local data density as an auxiliary self-supervised task to encode spatial distribution and location information.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By estimating the density of data points in local regions, the encoder learns to capture spatial irregularity and relative position cues, which are beneficial for tasks requiring location awareness.
mechanisms.math_structure: density_map = MLP(Encoder(x)); loss = MSE(density_map, ground_truth_local_density)
mechanisms.consequences: Adds an auxiliary prediction head and loss term; may introduce gradient competition with the main task; requires density ground truth which can be approximated via kernel density estimation.
anti_patterns: Using density prediction on uniformly dense data yields no benefit.
Ground truth density estimation with a fixed kernel may misalign with actual data distribution.

mechanisms.name: bi_directional_temporal_modeling
mechanisms.abstract_function: Predict a target point (e.g., goal) from an observed sequence, then generate future trajectories both forward (from current to target) and backward (from target to current) to enforce temporal consistency.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: A goal predictor produces a long-term target; two separate recurrent networks traverse time in opposite directions from start and goal respectively; their outputs are combined or compared to reduce ambiguity and improve prediction accuracy.
mechanisms.math_structure: \hat{g} = f_{\text{goal}}(\text{obs}); \quad \hat{y}_{1:T}^{\text{fwd}} = \text{GRU}_{\text{fwd}}(\text{obs}, \hat{g}); \quad \hat{y}_{1:T}^{\text{bwd}} = \text{GRU}_{\text{bwd}}(\hat{g}, \text{obs}); \quad \mathcal{L} = \sum \|\hat{y}^{\text{fwd}} - y\| + \sum \|\hat{y}^{\text{bwd}} - y\|.
mechanisms.consequences: Doubles the recurrent computation for each direction; requires a separate goal prediction module; may over-constrain outputs if goal is inaccurate.
anti_patterns: Using a deterministic goal leads to mode collapse in multi-modal scenarios.
Cannot leverage bidirectional consistency if the target point is missing or ill-defined.

mechanisms.name: geometric_structure_constraint
mechanisms.abstract_function: Enforce predictions of structured outputs (e.g., articulated poses, graphs) to satisfy known geometric relationships (bones, joint connections) via differentiable loss terms.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Define vectors or constraints based on ground-truth structural connectivity (e.g., parent-child joint pairs); compute L1/L2 differences between predicted and true geometric properties (bone length, endpoint chains, absolute joint positions); add these penalties to the main loss to guide the model toward physically plausible outputs.
mechanisms.math_structure: \mathcal{L}_{\text{bone}} = \sum_n \|\hat{B}_n - B_n\|_1; \quad \mathcal{L}_{\text{endpoint}} = \sum_{\text{chain}} \left\|\sum_{n \in \text{chain}}(\hat{J}_n - J_{\text{parent}(n)})\right\|; \quad \mathcal{L}_{\text{joint}} = \sum_n \|\hat{J}_n - J_n\|_1.
mechanisms.consequences: Adds extra hyperparameters to balance constraint terms; requires pre-defined structural graph of the output; may be sensitive to noisy ground-truth skeletons.
anti_patterns: Applying overly strict geometric constraints can suppress legitimate variability (e.g., natural body motion).
Using only endpoint loss without bone loss may ignore internal limb structure.

mechanisms.name: learnable_prototype_semantic_grouping
mechanisms.abstract_function: Cluster input features into a set of learnable prototypes via attention, producing compact semantic slots that represent coherent groups, enabling structured decomposition of complex scenes without human annotations.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Learnable prototypes act as soft cluster centroids; each input feature is soft-assigned to prototypes via attention weights, forming aggregated slots that capture recurring semantic patterns. These data-dependent slots then serve as inputs for contrastive learning, forcing the encoder to discriminate between distinct groups and thereby learn features that are both semantically meaningful and discriminative.
mechanisms.math_structure: Let F ∈ ℝ^(N×D) be features, P ∈ ℝ^(K×D) be learnable prototypes. Attention weights A = softmax(F P^T) ∈ ℝ^(N×K). Slots S = A^T F ∈ ℝ^(K×D). Contrastive loss is applied on S.
mechanisms.consequences: Adds K*D learnable parameters; slot quality depends on initialization and training stability; grouping may be noisy in early training; contrastive loss requires careful negative sampling.
anti_patterns: Fixing the number of prototypes may underfit or overfit scene complexity across datasets.
Grouping heavily relies on feature quality; poor initial features can lead to spurious grouping that harms representation learning.

mechanisms.name: global_false_negative_mining
mechanisms.abstract_function: Identifies and excludes samples with similar semantics from negative pairs in contrastive learning by dynamically learning per-anchor similarity thresholds across the entire dataset.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Learning a per-anchor similarity threshold enables global detection of false negatives (highly similar but semantically related samples) beyond the mini-batch. Excluding these samples from negative pairs prevents the model from pushing apart representations of similar semantics, leading to improved feature discrimination and representation quality.
mechanisms.math_structure: For each anchor x, learn threshold τ(x). Negative set N(x) = {z | sim(f(x), f(z)) < τ(x)}. τ(x) is optimized jointly with encoder f via contrastive loss, often using a differentiable objective that balances rejecting false negatives while retaining true negatives.
mechanisms.consequences: Introduces additional per-anchor parameters and online threshold optimization; requires efficient global similarity computation (e.g., via memory bank or approximate nearest neighbor) to keep cost independent of dataset size; risk of threshold collapse if not regularized.
anti_patterns: Setting thresholds too low may exclude many true negatives, harming discrimination ability.
Global similarity computation can become a bottleneck if not implemented with efficient indexing or caching strategies.

mechanisms.name: cluster_balanced_sampling
mechanisms.abstract_function: Remove semantically redundant samples from large-scale datasets by clustering and selecting representative samples per cluster, reducing data size while preserving performance and mitigating distribution shift.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Clustering groups semantically similar samples; selecting a subset (e.g., via uniform sampling per cluster) reduces redundancy and biases caused by imbalanced cluster sizes, leading to more efficient training with comparable generalization.
mechanisms.math_structure: Given teacher features Z, apply k-means to get clusters C; for each cluster c, sample N_c = min(N_target, |c|) samples uniformly or based on a density criterion; total sampled size reduced by 43.7%.
mechanisms.consequences: Sensitive to clustering quality and number of clusters; may discard rare but informative samples if not handled carefully.
anti_patterns: Using too few clusters may not capture semantic diversity; using too many clusters defeats redundancy reduction.

mechanisms.name: cluster_instance_discrimination
mechanisms.abstract_function: Transfer knowledge from a teacher model to a student model by jointly performing instance-level and cluster-level contrastive learning, enabling the student to learn both fine-grained and global semantic representations.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Instance contrast aligns individual features between teacher and student; cluster contrast aligns student features with teacher's cluster prototypes. This dual supervision forces the student to capture multi-granular semantics, improving representation quality.
mechanisms.math_structure: L = L_instance + λ * L_cluster, where L_instance = -log(exp(sim(z_s, z_t)/τ) / Σ exp(sim(z_s, z_i)/τ)), L_cluster = -log(exp(sim(z_s, p_c)/τ) / Σ exp(sim(z_s, p_j)/τ)) with p_c being teacher cluster prototype.
mechanisms.consequences: Requires pre-computed or online updated cluster prototypes, adding memory and computation; may be sensitive to cluster assignment quality; hyperparameter λ needs tuning.
anti_patterns: Using only instance discrimination may lose global structure; using only cluster discrimination may lose fine-grained details.

mechanisms.name: dual_encoder
mechanisms.abstract_function: Maps inputs from two different modalities into a shared embedding space using separate encoder networks, enabling cross-modal retrieval and alignment.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By employing two distinct encoders, each dedicated to its own modality, the model learns to project heterogeneous data into a common representation space. The contrastive loss function then pulls matched pairs together and pushes unmatched pairs apart, creating a joint embedding that supports zero-shot transfer across modalities.
mechanisms.math_structure: Let f: X → Z and g: Y → Z be two encoders. For a batch of N paired samples (x_i, y_i), the contrastive loss is: L = -1/N Σ_i log(exp(sim(f(x_i), g(y_i))/τ) / Σ_j exp(sim(f(x_i), g(y_j))/τ)), where sim is cosine similarity and τ is temperature.
mechanisms.consequences: Increases total parameter count and memory usage due to two separate encoder networks. Training with contrastive loss often requires large batch sizes and effective negative sampling strategies to avoid collapse. May also benefit from specialized data augmentations per modality.
anti_patterns: Using identical architectures for both modalities without adaptation may fail to capture modality-specific features. Poor negative sampling (e.g., too few negatives) can lead to representation collaps

mechanisms.name: capacity_aware_sequence_compression
mechanisms.abstract_function: Dynamically adjust the compression ratio of input sequences based on the capacity (e.g., parameter count or dimensionality) of the encoder, aiming to reduce computational cost while preserving representation quality.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Larger encoders have higher representational capacity and can capture essential information from a more compact input, so applying stronger compression (shorter sequence length) does not harm performance as much as for smaller encoders. Thus, conditioning compression rate on encoder capacity balances efficiency and accuracy.
mechanisms.math_structure: Let L be original sequence length, C be encoder capacity measure (e.g., hidden dim or parameter count). Define compression ratio r = α / C^β, where α, β > 0 are constants. Then compressed length L' = round(L * r).
mechanisms.consequences: Significant reduction in FLOPs and memory usage during training/inference, enabling scaling up to larger models with limited resources. However, overly aggressive compression may degrade performance, and the optimal compression strategy (e.g., mean pooling vs. attention pooling) varies with task and model.
anti_patterns: Using a fixed compression ratio regardless of encoder capacity may lead to suboptimal trade-offs (underfitting for large encoders or overfitting for small ones).
Choosing a compression strategy that is incompatible with the model architecture (e.g., attention pooling in transformers without proper adaptation) can cause training instability.

mechanisms.name: conditioned_projector
mechanisms.abstract_function: Injects auxiliary conditioning information (e.g., data augmentation parameters) into the projector network of a joint-embedding self-supervised learning framework, guiding the encoder to retain condition-specific information in representations while learning invariance to other factors.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By conditioning the projector on auxiliary signals (e.g., augmentation type), the encoder is forced to preserve those signals in its representations to solve the self-supervised task; this breaks the full invariance to augmentations and enables sensitivity to condition-relevant traits.
mechanisms.math_structure: Let f(x) be encoder, t be conditioning vector (e.g., one-hot of augmentation). Projector P(z|t) maps f(x) to representation z = P(f(x), t). SSL loss L = -log(exp(sim(z_i, z_j)/τ) / Σ) with z_i = P(f(x_i), t_i).
mechanisms.consequences: Increases projector capacity and inference cost; requires explicit knowledge or parsing of conditioning signals; may improve downstream tasks relying on condition-specific features but potentially hurt tasks where full invariance is beneficial.
anti_patterns: Using noisy or irrelevant conditioning signals that degrade representation quality.
Over-engineering conditioning that forces excessive sensitivity, destroying the benefits of invariance for generic downstream tasks.

mechanisms.name: nearest_neighbor_contrastive_learning
mechanisms.abstract_function: Enhances self-supervised representation learning by incorporating nearest-neighbor samples from the global dataset as additional positive pairs in contrastive learning, augmenting positive diversity beyond local augmentations.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Using nearest-neighbor samples as positives injects semantically related but visually distinct examples into the contrastive loss, forcing the encoder to learn features that capture broader inter-sample similarities, thus improving representation robustness and generalization.
mechanisms.math_structure: For each anchor sample x, find its nearest neighbor NN(x) in the embedding space. Loss = L_contrastive(x, augmented(x), NN(x)) where L_contrastive typically uses InfoNCE with positive pairs (x, NN(x)) and negative pairs (x, other samples).
mechanisms.consequences: Requires efficient approximate nearest neighbor search (e.g., FAISS) which adds memory and computation overhead; susceptible to inaccurate nearest neighbors under noisy or imbalanced data.
anti_patterns: Using nearest neighbors from a poorly initialized embedding can propagate noise and collapse representations.
Assuming simple Euclidean distance in raw feature space works without periodic re-clustering or momentum updates.

mechanisms.name: self_distillation
mechanisms.abstract_function: Learn representations by training a student network to match the output of a teacher network, where the teacher is a temporal ensemble or exponential moving average of the student.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: The teacher provides a stable, slowly evolving target, preventing representation collapse and encouraging the student to learn invariant features across different views or augmentations of the same input.
mechanisms.math_structure: Let student f_θ, teacher f_ξ (ξ = EMA(θ)). For augmented view x', target = f_ξ(x'), loss = ||f_θ(x) - target||² (stop-gradient on target).
mechanisms.consequences: Requires storing and updating an extra teacher model; may converge slower than contrastive methods; sensitive to the momentum coefficient.
anti_patterns: Teacher update momentum too high can stall learning; too low can cause instability.
Without careful augmentation design, the student may simply copy the teacher without learning meaningful representations.

mechanisms.name: universum_negative_sampling
mechanisms.abstract_function: Generates hard negative samples by incorporating universum (out-of-distribution) examples that lie outside any known class, enhancing discriminability in contrastive learning.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: Universum samples, being irrelevant to all classes, force the contrastive objective to push them farther away than random negatives, which tightens the decision boundary around positive pairs and yields more separable representations.
mechanisms.math_structure: L = -log( sim(z_i, z_j) / (sim(z_i, z_j) + sum_{k in neg} sim(z_i, z_k) + sum_{u in Universum} sim(z_i, z_u) ) )
mechanisms.consequences: Requires a separate set of universum data; may introduce extra computational cost for sampling and encoding; risk of over-regularization if universum is too close to actual negatives.
anti_patterns: Using in-domain random negatives as universum reduces the intended effect; universum must be clearly out-of-distribution.
Applying to tasks with very few classes may cause universum to overlap with actual classes.

mechanisms.name: frequency_temporal_augmentation
mechanisms.abstract_function: Generates positive pairs by jointly perturbing the frequency spectrum and the temporal structure of signals while preserving global temporal dynamics, improving representation robustness.
mechanisms.causal_behavior: By masking or distorting selected frequency components and applying temporal sub-sampling or warping, the augmentation creates views that preserve long-range temporal dependencies but vary in local details, forcing the encoder to learn higher-level temporal features invariant to spectral and temporal perturbations.
mechanisms.math_structure: x' = T( F^{-1}( M( F(x) ) ) ), where F is Fourier transform, M is frequency mask, T is temporal augmentation (e.g., subsequence sampling or jittering).
mechanisms.consequences: Increases training time due to additional transforms; may destroy periodic patterns if frequency mask is too aggressive; requires careful tuning of perturbation strength.
anti_patterns: Applying uniform frequency masking without considering domain-specific periodicities can break temporal coherence.
Using only time-domain augmentation (e.g., cropping) without frequency perturbation fails to capture spectral invariances.

mechanisms.name: decoupled_st_masked_pretraining
mechanisms.abstract_function: 把空间轴与时间轴解耦分别做掩码重建预训练, 学得可注入下游预测器的长程纯净时空表示
mechanisms.causal_behavior: 空间轴整传感器遮罩 + 时间轴 patch 遮罩分两支各自重建 → 避免时空混合遮罩造成的互泄答案 (任务过易) → 两轴各得纯化表征 → 长窗预训练表示经 skip 注入下游各层, 短窗预测也享长程信息
mechanisms.math_structure: 空间支: mask 整个传感器 i 的全部时间步 x_{i,:}, 时空自编码器重建; 时间支: 长窗 T_long=864 切 patch 随机遮 25% 重建; loss = 仅掩码位的 MAE; 下游: 预训练 encoder 第 l 层表示 h_l 经线性投影加到预测器对应层 (skip injection)
mechanisms.consequences: 长窗 T_long=864 上注意力 O(T²) 预训练算力代价大; 双分支两份预训练开销; 掩码率 0.25 需按数据集调

evidence.delta: STD-MAE 17.80 达 SOTA (长窗解耦预训练)

anti_patterns: 时空混合遮罩 (同时遮空间+时间) 反而有害——轴间互泄答案使任务太易, 表征退化
下游只微调不做 skip 注入会浪费长窗预训练的长程信息优势

mechanisms.name: masked_attention_variants
mechanisms.abstract_function: 把多种掩码模式直接做进注意力内部并行训练, 强制表示同时捕获局部拓扑/长程相似/因果时序多方依赖
mechanisms.causal_behavior: 6 种注意力掩码变体并行 (随机/管状/块状/短程图 hop/长程 DTW 相似节点/未来时间) → 每种掩码强制注意力在特定缺失模式下重建 → 拼接多变体表示 → 局部性/长程性/因果性同时编码进表示
mechanisms.math_structure: 对每种掩码 m∈{random,tube,block,k-hop,DTW,future}: h_m = softmax(QKᵀ/√d + M_m) V, M_m∈{0,-inf} 掩码矩阵; h = W_o·concat(h_1..h_6); 各变体配重建损失作用于被掩位
mechanisms.consequences: 6 路并行注意力算力/显存约 6×; 变体间冗余需正则; DTW 相似度需离线预计算

evidence.delta: 声称 17.06 超 STD-MAE; 截至 2026-07 未见独立复现, 存疑

anti_patterns: 变体堆叠收益边际递减而成本线性涨, 需消融选子集
声称数字未经独立复现, 移植前务必小规模验证

mechanisms.name: adaptive_st_embedding
mechanisms.abstract_function: 用无语义的可学习时空嵌入张量直接加在输入上, 让模型数据自适应地区分每个节点与时刻的身份
mechanisms.causal_behavior: 可学习张量 E_adp∈R^{N×T×d} 加在输入投影上 → 每个 (节点,时刻) 获数据驱动的独特身份 → 无需人工设计 tod/dow 语义即可打破不可区分性 → vanilla transformer 即达 SOTA
mechanisms.math_structure: X' = Linear(X) + E_adp; E_adp∈R^{N×T_in×d} 纯可学习参数 (不查表/无语义/不手工设计); 后接普通 spatial/temporal attention 层
mechanisms.consequences: 参数量 N×T×d 比查表式嵌入大; 对训练中未见过的新节点/新时刻无泛化 (zero-shot 差); 几乎不增算力

evidence.delta: STAEformer 18.22; 去掉该嵌入劣化约 +19%

anti_patterns: 与手工 tod/dow 嵌入叠加易冗余——STAEformer 证明可学习版可完全替代手工版
节点数/时间步很大时 N×T×d 参数膨胀

mechanisms.name: parameterfree_graph_propagation
mechanisms.abstract_function: 用无参数的固定图传播算子保留多个阶次的邻域聚合, 以零参数代价补足注意力缺失的局部高阶信息
mechanisms.causal_behavior: 归一化邻接 L̂ 的 1..K 阶幂次直接乘特征 (SGC 式) → 显式保留局部高阶聚合 → 与注意力的全局自适应聚合拼接互补 → 局部高阶 × 全局自适应双通道各补其短
mechanisms.math_structure: H_k = L̂^k X (k=1..K), L̂ = D^{-1/2}(A+I)D^{-1/2}; 输出 = W·concat(H_1..H_K, Attn(X)); 传播无参数, 稀疏 L̂ 幂次可预计算
mechanisms.consequences: L̂^k 需预计算 (稀疏图便宜, 幂次稠化后内存涨); K 过大则过平滑; 无参数表达力上限低, 单靠它不够需与注意力组合

evidence.delta: STGformer 中无参数图传播支路与注意力组合优于纯注意力基线

anti_patterns: 阶次 K 过大→过平滑退化, 节点表示趋同
稠密大图上 L̂^k 稠化内存爆炸, 需保持稀疏存储

mechanisms.name: shared_qkv_st_attention
mechanisms.abstract_function: 时间维与空间维共享同一组 Q/K/V 投影, 转置输入即得两种注意力, 配线性注意力把时空二次复杂度降到线性
mechanisms.causal_behavior: 同一组 W_Q,W_K,W_V 同时作用于 X∈R^{T×N×d} 及其转置 → 参数共享把时空注意力压进同一语义空间 → 核化线性注意力后 O(TN²+NT²) 降为 O((N+T)d²) → 大图长窗可负担
mechanisms.math_structure: 时间注意力: 沿 T 轴 A_t = φ(Q)(φ(K)ᵀV); 空间注意力: X 转置后复用同一组投影沿 N 轴同理; φ 为核特征映射 (如 elu(x)+1); Q,K,V 投影矩阵两维共享
mechanisms.consequences: 共享投影牺牲部分维度特化表达力; 线性注意力核近似损失 softmax 精度; 需分母归一化防数值不稳

evidence.delta: 比 STAEformer 快约 100× (共享 QKV + 线性注意力)

anti_patterns: 精度敏感任务上核化线性注意力近似退化, 需对照 softmax 版消融
T/N 各学各的投影会回到 O(TN²+NT²), 大图上不可负担

mechanisms.name: frozen_backbone_router
mechanisms.abstract_function: 冻结多个已训练骨干模型, 只训练图条件轻量路由器按输入加权融合各骨干输出, 极低成本稳定涨点
mechanisms.causal_behavior: 多骨干各自捕获不同模式 → 图条件路由器按输入/图结构生成融合权重 → 冻结骨干避免微调破坏已学知识 → 仅 ~17K 参数即获稳定集成增益, 超单模型与均匀平均
mechanisms.math_structure: ŷ = Σ_i g_i(G, x)·f_i(x); f_i 为冻结骨干 (不反传); g = softmax(MLP([pool(x); pool(A)])) 为图条件路由器 (~17K 参数); 训练只更新 g
mechanisms.consequences: 需先训练/集齐多个骨干 (前期成本); 推理时全部骨干前向, 算力 = Σ骨干; 路由器在小验证集上可能过拟合

evidence.delta: 稳定超过任一单模型与均匀平均融合

anti_patterns: 骨干同质化 (各骨干相似) 时路由器无增益, 需骨干多样性
解冻骨干联合微调即破坏'稳定'这一核心优势

mechanisms.name: spatial_axis_ssm_scan
mechanisms.abstract_function: 把选择性状态空间扫描沿传感器轴运行并配局部卷积门控支路, 以线性复杂度建模空间维长程传播
mechanisms.causal_behavior: 传感器按启发式/可学习顺序排成序列 → Mamba selective scan 沿传感器轴递推 (输入相关 B,C,Δ) → 局部卷积门控支路补短程邻域 → 线性复杂度下获得跨传感器长程传播
mechanisms.math_structure: 排序 π 后序列 x_{π(1..N)}: h_i = Ā(Δ_i) h_{i-1} + B̄(x_i) x_i, y_i = C(x_i) h_i; 并行支路 y'_i = σ(Conv1d(x_i)) ⊙ y_i; 输出按 π 逆映射回图
mechanisms.consequences: 交通域精度增益边际 (ST-Mamba 仅约 0.16%), 主要价值在长序列/大图效率; 传感器排序 π 无自然定义, 不同排法结果有差; 双向扫描成本翻倍

evidence.delta: ST-Mamba 精度增益仅约 0.16% (边际), 价值在效率

anti_patterns: 期待精度大幅提升会落空——移植动机应是效率而非精度
随意打乱传感器顺序会破坏空间局部性, 排序需依图结构

mechanisms.name: soft_node_grouping_mixing
mechanisms.abstract_function: 用 softmax 可学习分配把节点软分组为宏节点, 在宏节点空间用多项式基做 token mixing 后映射回节点
mechanisms.causal_behavior: 可学习分配 S = softmax(Θ)∈R^{N×M} 把 N 节点软聚合为 M 宏节点 → 宏节点间用 KAN 式多项式基 mixing → 逆映射回节点 → 分组归纳偏置压缩空间自由度并显式建模簇结构
mechanisms.math_structure: Z = SᵀX (N→M); Z' = Σ_k a_k·B_k(Z), B_k 为多项式/样条基 (KAN 式); X' = S Z'; S = softmax(Θ), Θ∈R^{N×M} 可学习
mechanisms.consequences: 作者自认提升 modest; 软分配引入 N×M 额外参数; 宏节点数 M 需调; 多项式基阶数过高易不稳

evidence.delta: STKAN 提升 modest (作者自述)

anti_patterns: 硬分派 (argmax) 不可微, 需保持 soft 或加温度退火
期待大幅涨点不现实——提升 modest 是作者原话

mechanisms.name: state_dependent_memory_kernel
mechanisms.abstract_function: 把分数阶导数的固定幂律记忆核替换为依赖当前状态的注意力核, 让长记忆的衰减方式随系统状态自适应
mechanisms.causal_behavior: 分数阶模型记忆核为固定幂律 (t-τ)^{-α} 不可调 → 换成依赖状态的注意力核 K(t,τ,x(t),x(τ)) → 记忆窗口随状态伸缩 → 漂移/突变期自动缩短记忆, 平稳期放长
mechanisms.math_structure: 替换分数阶固定核: x'(t) = ∫ K_θ(t,τ,x(t),x(τ)) f(x(τ)) dτ, K_θ = softmax_τ( q(x(t))·k(x(τ)) ); 离散化为历史状态的自适应加权和
mechanisms.consequences: 核依赖状态后失去闭式/FFT 加速, 计算更贵; 注意力核需 warmup 防早期梯度不稳; 理论保证弱于固定幂律核

evidence.delta: STG-FADE 自适应长记忆核超固定幂律核

anti_patterns: 完全丢弃幂律归纳偏置在极长记忆场景可能退化, 可保留幂律作初始化
状态相关核不 warmup 易训练早期发散

mechanisms.name: delay_differential_modeling
mechanisms.abstract_function: 用延迟微分方程显式建模节点间影响传播的时空延迟, 替代即时耦合假设使动力学贴合物理传播过程
mechanisms.causal_behavior: 交通流影响从传感器 j 传到 i 有物理延迟 τ_ij → DDE dx_i/dt = f(x_i(t), Σ_j A_ij x_j(t-τ_ij)) 显式建模 → 比即时 ODE/GNN 更贴合传播物理 → 长程预测更准
mechanisms.math_structure: dx_i/dt = f_θ(x_i(t), Σ_{j∈N(i)} A_ij g_θ(x_j(t-τ_ij))); τ_ij 可学习或按距离/速度估计; 需历史缓冲 H 取延迟值, 数值求解步长 < min τ
mechanisms.consequences: 需维护历史缓冲 (内存↑); τ 可学习时优化面不光滑; 求解步长受最小延迟约束, 长仿真成本高

evidence.delta: STDDE 18.11

anti_patterns: 延迟 τ 全学成 0 则退化为即时模型, 失去建模意义——需初始化/正则防塌缩
历史缓冲太短会截断长延迟依赖

mechanisms.name: future_query_periodic_attention
mechanisms.abstract_function: 用未来时刻的周期时间码作 query、历史表示作 key 的跨注意力, 把预测转化为周期条件检索以增强零样本迁移
mechanisms.causal_behavior: 未来 tod/dow 嵌入作 query, 历史 patch 表示作 key/value → 注意力按周期相位对齐检索历史相似模式 → 不依赖目标域标注即可迁移 → zero-shot 接近全数据训练
mechanisms.math_structure: q_f = E_tod(t_f) + E_dow(d_f); A = softmax(q_f K_hᵀ/√d); ŷ_f = A·V_h; K_h,V_h 来自历史 patch transformer; 配 instance norm 抗幅值漂移
mechanisms.consequences: 依赖周期假设, 非周期突发事件弱; query 只含时间码时表达力受限于周期码区分度

evidence.delta: OpenCity zero-shot 与全数据 SOTA 差距 <8%

anti_patterns: 周期码粒度太粗 (如只到小时) 时 query 碰撞, 检索退化
不做归一化时跨域幅值差异破坏周期检索

mechanisms.name: multi_strategy_patch_pretraining
mechanisms.abstract_function: 在 patch 级用多种掩码策略并行预训练时空表示, 再以 prompt 学习低成本适配不同下游数据布局
mechanisms.causal_behavior: patch 化统一不同数据集形状 → 4 种掩码策略并行预训练 → 多策略互补覆盖不同冗余/尺度模式 → prompt 学习适配下游 → 单模型跨数据集泛化
mechanisms.math_structure: X∈R^{N×T} → M 个 patch token; 策略集 {m_1..m_4} 各采样掩码模式; loss = Σ_s λ_s·recon(visible_s → masked_s); 下游: 可学习 prompt token 拼前缀, 只训 prompt + 头部
mechanisms.consequences: 多策略预训练成本 × 策略数; patch 形状跨数据集对齐需插值/重采样; prompt 容量有限, 复杂下游欠拟合

evidence.delta: UniST 跨数据集 zero/few-shot 有效

anti_patterns: 单一掩码策略对多形态数据覆盖不足——多策略互补是关键
prompt 太短在差异大的下游欠拟合

mechanisms.name: correlation_adaptive_augmentation
mechanisms.abstract_function: 按区域间相关性自适应设定 Bernoulli 掩码概率并配路网拓扑增强, 让自监督增强难度匹配局部数据结构
mechanisms.causal_behavior: 高相关区域的传感器太易被重建 (任务太易) → 按区域相关矩阵上调该区域掩码概率 + 路网删/加边扰动 → 增强难度与局部冗余匹配 → SSL 信号在空间上更均匀有效
mechanisms.math_structure: p_i = clip(p_0 + α·corr̄_i), corr̄_i 为节点 i 与邻域平均相关; 掩码 M_i ~ Bernoulli(p_i); 路网增强: 沿邻接 A 随机删/加边扰动
mechanisms.consequences: 需预计算区域相关矩阵, 分布漂移时需重估; 概率自适应增加调参维度

evidence.delta: SSL-STMFormer 消融中相关自适应增强有正贡献

anti_patterns: 全局统一掩码率在高异质网络上难度失衡 (高相关区太易/低相关区太难)
相关矩阵须只用训练段估计, 防测试信息泄漏

mechanisms.name: soft_cluster_heterogeneity_ssl
mechanisms.abstract_function: 用软聚类分配作辅助自监督任务, 让表示显式承载空间异质性的簇结构
mechanisms.causal_behavior: 节点表示经 soft 簇分配 (可学习簇心) → 辅助任务约束分配一致性 → 表示被迫编码'属于哪类行为模式' → 空间异质性结构化为可寻址的簇
mechanisms.math_structure: s_i = softmax(h_i Cᵀ/τ), C∈R^{K×d} 可学习簇心; 辅助损失 = 簇内对比一致性 + 分配熵正则 (防坍缩); 与主 SSL 损失加权求和
mechanisms.consequences: 簇数 K 需先验; 辅助任务与主任务权重需平衡; 无正则时簇易坍缩

evidence.delta: SSL-STMFormer 消融中软聚类辅助任务有正贡献

anti_patterns: 无防坍缩正则 (分配熵/均匀性) 时所有节点挤进一簇
K 取错把连续行为谱强行切块, 反伤表示

mechanisms.name: region_city_contrastive
mechanisms.abstract_function: 在区域与城市两个尺度上做表征对比, 用跨尺度一致性锚定时间异质性
mechanisms.causal_behavior: 同节点在区域尺度与城市尺度两视图表征 → InfoNCE 拉近跨尺度正对、推远负对 → 表示同时含局部细节与全局上下文 → 不同时段的异质模式被跨尺度锚定
mechanisms.math_structure: z_r = pool_region(h), z_c = pool_city(h); L = -log exp(sim(z_rⁱ,z_cⁱ)/τ) / Σ_j exp(sim(z_rⁱ,z_cʲ)/τ) (InfoNCE)
mechanisms.consequences: 双尺度编码两份前向成本; 批量小时负样本不足对比退化; 尺度层级划分依赖先验

evidence.delta: SSL-STMFormer 消融中区域-城市对比有正贡献

anti_patterns: 两尺度视图同源无差异时对比退化为恒等映射
批量太小负样本不足, InfoNCE 信号弱

mechanisms.name: scale_conditioned_expert_mixing
mechanisms.abstract_function: 把不同时间尺度的模式分给不同专家子网处理并按尺度条件路由, 用条件计算解耦多尺度异质动态
mechanisms.causal_behavior: 输入经尺度描述子路由到对应尺度专家 (趋势/周期/瞬态) → 各专家专精单一尺度动态 → 门控按尺度证据加权融合 → 避免单网络在冲突尺度目标间梯度互相干扰
mechanisms.math_structure: y = Σ_i g_i(x)·E_i(x); g = softmax(W·s(x)), s(x) 为尺度描述子 (多分辨率统计/频带能量); E_i 为尺度专精子网 (不同 kernel 宽/膨胀率/周期偏置); 可加 top-k 稀疏化与负载均衡损失
mechanisms.consequences: 专家数 × 子网参数; top-k 路由负载不均需均衡损失; 尺度描述子设计不当则路由坍缩到单专家

evidence.delta: MoE 式条件计算在时序基础模型 (Time-MoE 等) 验证有效
evidence.source: B6 概念综合: MoE × 多尺度时序 (Time-MoE ICLR'25 佐证)

anti_patterns: 路由退化到单专家等于白加容量——需负载均衡正则
尺度描述子与数据真实尺度错位时专家学不到专精
mechanisms.provenance: B6 概念综合 (2026-07 调研): MoE 思想 × 多尺度时序, 补 multi_scale+heterogeneity+sequential_order 检索缺口
